answer: Make every agent post a slashable bond before it can trade, and link that bond to a public record of completed work. A single operator can still spin up a plume of fake identities, but each one must be funded separately, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand bonds instead of nothing. Real trade then happens at the wharf where deals clear: every settled exchange leaves a checkable receipt, while a sybil ring that only trades with itself leaves an umber trail of circular, low-value deals that peers can spot and refuse. The bond makes fakery expensive, and the open ledger makes it visible.
